page: Amazon Web Services r7i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside a 105 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions).

Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Accelerator hardware is absent, providing zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive single-core execution alongside predictable constraints in highly parallelized compute. The single-core Geekbench score reached 1829.0 and stress-ng recorded 2008.49, falling into the middle 50% percentile across evaluated systems. Conversely, multi-core throughput registered in the bottom 25%, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 4038.0 and stress-ng multi-core yielding 4002.86. Memory bandwidth measured 24.76 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 25.14 GB/sec for writes.

Performance profiles show stable efficiency for memory-centric utilities and lightweight serving tasks, generating 7.0 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. In caching and database tests, PassMark database operations scored 2297.03 and Redis SET operations achieved 4.83 million operations per second, both sitting in the bottom 25% due to the four-vCPU hardware ceiling. The server is well positioned for memory-intensive enterprise applications, caching tiers, medium relational databases, and microservices requiring significant DDR5 capacity without demanding extensive parallel CPU throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services r7i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Running on the AWS Nitro System, it allocates 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes local storage and GPUs, relying on remote network storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate consistent mid-tier single-core CPU execution, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1829.0, while multi-threaded capabilities remain limited by the low core count. The instance is suited for memory-bound workloads such as in-memory databases, Redis caches, and enterprise web backends needing generous DDR5 allocations.
